TR «yani onların dualarına» translates that text, not a correction. Rest (fāʿil reading with Anfāl 24, sīn of ṭalab, implied lām) is accurate.

J1.evidence: Source reads «ويُجيب اللَّهُ الذين آمنوا أي: دعاهم». TR 'onların dualarına' reads it as دعاءَهم (their supplication). That is almost certainly the intended sense, since the hamza is often dropped in this text, but it differs from the literal 'He called them' and has no note. A scholar should decide whether a [Mütercim notu] is needed.

J2.evidence: On «دعاهم» (= دعاءَهم, their supplication) the EN «when they call Him» is acceptable, so the reviewer's point is not the defect. But the EN transliterates the Arabic phrase «للذين آمنوا» as «[li-lladhīna āmanū]» in Latin letters (a Quranic wording; must stay in Arabic script), and drops the Arabic of verse 3973, giving English only (glossary_en rule 3).

J1.evidence: Besides rendering «أي: دعاهم» as 'when they call Him' without a note, EN transliterates the Quranic phrase in Latin: '[li-lladhīna āmanū]' for «ويستجيب الله للذين آمنوا». That is a binding-standard error; it must stay in Arabic script.
